subject.title: [Refactor] Standardize retry backoff strategies across all external HTTP integrations

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a cross-cutting retry-policy abstraction, or retain owner-specific retry behavior until concrete failing integrations establish a shared invariant?
rationale: The report requests a broad behavioral refactor without defining retry-safe operations, error classifications, or the compatibility contract for existing integrations.

options.title: Require a narrow proposal
options.body: Ask for one reproduced integration problem, its upstream retry contract, and a pilot design before approving shared infrastructure.

options.title: Adopt a global policy
options.body: Sponsor a design that inventories every affected integration and explicitly defines idempotency, Retry-After, cancellation, and observability rules.

options.title: Keep local ownership
options.body: Retain integration-specific retry implementations unless future evidence shows a reusable core contract.

recommendation.title: Require a narrow proposal
recommendation.body: Ask for one reproduced integration problem, its upstream retry contract, and a pilot design before approving shared infrastructure.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the current proposal and can refine it into a concrete, reviewable contract; current-main area ownership was not established.
